beginAutonomyPollingAssessment.whatTheBytesActuallyShow: Both occurrences are the definition and its call site, and the definition is the real loop, not a stub: beginAutonomyPolling = () => { if (autonomyPollTimer !== null) clearInterval(autonomyPollTimer); const tick = () => { if (runRegistry.activeRuns().length === 0) return; lastReconciliation = runReconciliation(); ... }; autonomyPollTimer = setInterval(tick, options.autonomyPollIntervalMs ?? 5e3); autonomyPollTimer.unref?.(); }. deliberatelyAttendedAssessment.question: Is deliberatelyAttended sufficient to keep a falsification receipt from reading as a genuine failure?
deliberatelyAttendedAssessment.theDeeperGap: Four receipts were produced inside fifteen minutes by at least three different versions of the driver: 10:16 without deliberatelyAttended, 10:25 and 10:27 with it but before the timestamp fix, 10:31 after both. Nothing in any receipt says which driver produced it. bindCandidate recomputes the candidate so a receipt cannot be reattributed by being moved, but the same standard is not applied to the instrument: there is no driver source digest, no script version, no git revision in the receipt. That is the one structural gap this reviewer would close next, and it subsumes the deliberatelyAttended gap.
deliberatelyAttendedAssessment.theGapItExposes: It is absent from docs/omega/2026-07-26-omega-fa07-rc18-gate2-unattended-first-observation.json, generated at 10:16:24Z, because that run predates the field. So one of the four receipts is still distinguishable only by its filename -- the exact condition the field was added to end -- and it is one of the two greens the packet leans on. A reader today infers its intent from field ABSENCE, which is the weakest possible signal and indistinguishable from an older or a truncated writer.
deliberatelyAttendedAssessment.verdict: SUFFICIENT FOR THE ARTIFACTS THAT CARRY IT, AND CORRECTLY MOTIVATED. Not yet sufficient across the packet, for a reason the field itself exposes.
deliberatelyAttendedAssessment.whatItGetsRight: The principle is the one the packet already applies with bindCandidate: an artifact must not depend on where it is filed to be read correctly. Two fields rather than one (deliberatelyAttended and isFalsificationControl), emitted before the attribution block, sourced directly from options.falsifyAttended so they cannot disagree with what the run did. On the four receipts it is present in, a reader who saw only the JSON would classify each correctly.

theArchitecturalFindingTheReviewerIsObli.consequenceForTheNewEvidence: Cuts both ways, and the producer should not be credited with more than it earned. Because the engine bundle is byte-identical across rc15, rc16, rc17 and rc18 (6922c83e05c89bc7..., recomputed here from the installed app and from the read-only mount), re-driving gate 2 on rc18 exercises the same engine bytes rc15 did. What it genuinely adds is that the run provably came out of the rc18 candidate rather than being carried on an argument. What it does not add -- and what no run of this driver can add -- is any observation of the +829/+489/+277-line rc18 Full Auto host surfaces (issue31_delivery.rs, omega_router.rs, agent_panel.rs) that the rc18 receipt was worried about. Those remain unexercised on every candidate.
theArchitecturalFindingTheReviewerIsObli.consequenceForTheRc18Receipt: The rc18 receipt's stated reason for refusing gate 2 was that framedCallsDuringSilentWindow counts 'traffic across the real host bridge', making the observation host-level. That premise is incorrect: those are the driver's own stdio calls to the engine, and the 'host' is a stand-in in the same Node process. The rc18 receipt itself established the correct characterisation twice elsewhere -- for gate 5 ('its host stand-in answers append_system_note itself and never reaches crates/agent_ui/src/omega_host_bridge.rs') and for gates 3 to 9 ('Because the driver uses a TypeScript host stand-in, these re-observations are engine-level in character'). It applied that rule correctly to gates 1, 3-9 and incorrectly to gate 2. Gate 2's evidence was engine-level all along; the rc15 hostBinaryDigest was provenance for which bundle the engine came out of, not a claim that the host ran.
theArchitecturalFindingTheReviewerIsObli.finding: This driver never executes the rc18 host binary. bindCandidate() hashes Contents/MacOS/omega for provenance and then startEngine() spawns Contents/Resources/omega-effectd/bin/omega-effectd, a four-line /bin/sh shim that execs the bundled node against dist/omega-effectd.mjs. Everything on the host side of the protocol -- resolve_workspace, create_thread, dispatch_turn, refresh_evidence, append_system_note -- is answered by a TypeScript stand-in inside the driver process (fa07-installed-gates.ts onHostRequest). The Rust bridge in crates/agent_ui/src/omega_host_bridge.rs is not in the path.
theArchitecturalFindingTheReviewerIsObli.whyThisIsNeverthelessAcceptance: Applied consistently, the rc18 receipt's own standard admits this. It accepted gates 3, 4, 6, 7 and 9 as 'genuinely re-observed on rc18, not inherited' while recording that they are engine-level in character because of the same stand-in. Gate 2 now meets exactly that bar, with more behind it than most of them: live providers, twelve real Codex executions, a 240-second window, a repeat observation and a falsification control. Accepting gates 3-9 on that basis and refusing gate 2 alone would be the same inconsistency in reverse. The residual -- that no gate in this packet has been observed through the Rust host -- is a packet-wide residual, not a gate-2 blocker, and it is recorded below as such.

theRestartClaim.verdict: SUPPORTED, and it is a real process restart, not a reconnect.
theRestartClaim.why: The driver's 'return' calls client.stop(), which sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL if the child has not exited (fa07-installed-gates.ts, stop()), then calls startEngine(binding.enginePath, dataRoot, policyB, 2), which spawns a fresh engine process at generation 2 over the same data root and re-issues initialize. Everything asserted afterwards is read from that new process: runSurvivedReturn true, stateAfterReturn 'cap_reached' equal to the pre-restart state, turnCountAfterReturn 9 equal to the pre-restart 9, reportSurvivedReturn true with 9 turns, receiptObjectiveDigestMatches true against sha256 of the objective, durableStateOnDisk true. The claim 'all 9 turns, report, receipt and objective intact' is what the fields say.

recommendations: Record the driver's source revision in every receipt it writes -- a digest of the script, or the commit it was run from. Four receipts in fifteen minutes came from three driver versions and no artifact says so. This is bindCandidate's own principle applied to the instrument, and it subsumes the deliberatelyAttended back-fill problem.

Include outputDigest in the gate-2 receipt's providerInvocations mapping. It is already computed and already public-safe, and without it exit 0 plus a length is not checkable evidence that a turn did work.
Pair provider invocations to turnRefs so everyTurnHadAProvider tests what its name says instead of comparing two totals.

Decide whether a terminal run's durable report should reconcile the turns that completed after the cap bound. Today a finished cap_reached run permanently reports nine turns for twelve turns of executed work, in the report as well as the projection.
Correct the falsify-branch comment 'Everything else about the run is identical'; the control ran a 125 s window against the observation's 240 s.

For any future candidate, take one gate through the real GPUI host. Every gate in this packet is engine-level, and the packet's own falsifier speaks of an installed Omega journey. The rc18 receipt's suggestion -- a visual_test_runner scene -- is the cheapest route and needs no owner involvement.

timestampDefectAssessment.onKeepingTheFailingReceipt: docs/omega/2026-07-26-omega-fa07-rc18-gate2-boundary-defect-observation.json records framedCallsDuringSilentWindow 1 naming get_run, silentWindowWasSilent false, alongside writeCallsAfterStart 0 and a completed 12-attempt run. Keeping it is correct and the reviewer endorses it: it is the only artifact that shows the gate was a coin-flip on scheduler timing rather than a property, and deleting it would have left the fix looking like a tidy-up.
timestampDefectAssessment.question: Can the boundary defect reproduce under the new logic?
timestampDefectAssessment.theDefect: callsDuringSilence filtered audited.calls on entry.at >= silenceStart && entry.at <= silenceEnd. auditClient.call pushes {method, at: Date.now()} at the instant a call is SENT, and returns the promise for the reply; silenceStart is read after that reply has been awaited. When the final get_run of the wait loop returned inside the same millisecond it was sent, its recorded 'at' equalled silenceStart and the inclusive comparison counted a call made before the window as one made during it.
timestampDefectAssessment.theDirectionOfTheOldDefectMatters: Worth stating because it changes how the earlier greens should be read. The new set is a strict subset of the old set: any call appended after the snapshot necessarily has at >= silenceStart. So the defect could only OVER-count -- turn a silent run red -- and could never under-count a call into invisibility. It could not have manufactured a green. The 10:16 first observation, produced before the fix, reported 0 under the looser rule and therefore reports 0 under the stricter one as well. Its green stands.
timestampDefectAssessment.theFix: callsAtSilenceStart = audited.calls.length is snapshotted at silenceStart, and callsDuringSilence = audited.calls.slice(callsAtSilenceStart). Counting is by position in an append-only log.
timestampDefectAssessment.verdict: NO. The fix is sound, and it is a stronger kind of fix than the defect strictly required.
whyItCannotReproduce: auditClient.call is the sole appender to audited.calls; nothing else in the module writes to that array. client.stop() and client.waitForIdle() bypass the audit entirely, and neither is invoked inside the window.

Between the last await in the wait loop (line 221) and the snapshot (line 231) every statement is synchronous -- three counts, a Date.now(), a length read. Node is single-threaded and there is no pending continuation that could append an entry in that gap, so the snapshot cannot miss a call already sent.

Inbound engine-to-host requests are recorded on policy.trace with their own clock and never touch audited.calls, so engine activity during the window cannot contaminate the count. This is what lets the same receipt report 0 driver calls and 12 engine dispatches without contradiction.

slice() over an append-only array is an identity on 'appended after the snapshot'. There is no clock in it, so there is no boundary to be on the wrong side of. Date.now() survives only in silentWindowMs, which is reported as a measured duration and is not an input to any assertion.

turnCountLagAssessment.aRelatedWeakField: everyTurnHadAProvider is computed as invocations.filter(ok).length >= turnsAtEnd.length. Under lag that is 12 >= 9, which is true for reasons unrelated to whether any particular turn had a provider. The field is sound in intent -- 'a turn that no provider executed is not a turn' -- but as written it cannot detect the failure it names. It should pair invocations to turnRefs.
turnCountLagAssessment.onTheCapArgument: ACCEPTED. Binding the cap to acceptance is the correct choice and the producer's reasoning for it is right: if the cap were evaluated against observed turns, a run could dispatch a thirteenth and fourteenth turn whenever evidence lagged, which converts a safety bound into a suggestion. A cap must bind the thing it is protecting against -- work dispatched -- not the thing that reports on it.
turnCountLagAssessment.question: Is the producer's explanation of turnCount < successfulAttempts sound?
turnCountLagAssessment.theMechanismConfirmedInSource: The stand-in replies {accepted: true} to dispatch_turn immediately and then runs the provider asynchronously (fa07-installed-gates.ts: 'Accept first, execute after: the engine's dispatch contract is accept-then-observe-through-evidence, exactly like the GPUI host'), pushing the turn record only when the provider returns. The engine increments successfulAttempts on acceptance and projects turns from refresh_evidence polling. Once successfulAttempts reaches turnCap the run is terminal, and a terminal run stops being reconciled, so the last turns to complete are never projected in. Hence 12 accepted, 12 executed, 7-9 projected.
turnCountLagAssessment.verdict: SOUND AS TO THE CAP. INCOMPLETE AS TO THE FINAL RECORD, which the explanation does not reach.
turnCountLagAssessment.whatTheArgumentDoesNotCover: Why the FINAL record is allowed to keep under-reporting after the work is done. The driver waits for every provider to finish (waitForIdle to inFlight == 0) and re-reads the run, and the count is still 9 of 12. The durable report agrees at 9, so the under-count is not a display artefact -- it is what the run's permanent record says. A person opening a finished cap_reached run sees nine turns for twelve turns of work. Nothing in gate 2 asks about that, and it does not weaken any gate-2 assertion (the assertions are turns > 0 across the window and turns >= 3), so it is recorded as a finding rather than a disagreement.
